references.text: The same exhortation to fear God in connection with how one treats one's neighbor, using the identical expression וְיָרֵאתָ מֵּאֱלֹהֶיךָ
A nearby verse that also uses the verb תוֹנוּ (to exploit/oppress) in the context of trade between Israelites
The same chapter with a repetition of the exhortation to fear God (וְיָרֵאתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶיךָ) regarding the treatment of poor brothers
An additional exhortation in the same chapter to fear God concerning the treatment of servants
The fundamental command to love one's neighbor as oneself, which underlies the prohibition against exploiting one's fellow citizen
Prohibition against oppressing (תוֹנֶה) foreigners, using the same Hebrew root as in Lev 25:17
A prophetic warning against oppressing one another, using the same expression אִישׁ אֶת־אָחִיו
An exhortation not to harbor evil thoughts toward one's neighbor, parallel to the prohibition against exploiting one's fellow citizen
An exhortation not to exploit workers, based on the same ethical principle of fair treatment
